findings.review_scope: Registered-source content review of arXiv:2202.06117v4, stamped 27 February 2024, by Paromita Dubey, Yaqing Chen and Hans-Georg Müller. The PDF has 73 pages; main text ends after Funding on shared page 33 above the SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL heading at y=106.52787780761719. Fresh text covers pages 1-32 and the main-text portion of page 33. Only the supplement heading was inspected in a separate crop. No embedded supplement body or later references were read.
findings.inventory: Seven actual THEOREM headings occur: 4.1 on page 11; 5.1 on 12; 5.2 on 13; 5.3 on 14; 6.1 and 6.2 on 17; 6.3 on 18. Complete statements were compared visually with the PDF. Proposition 1, citations and supplement results are excluded.
original_statements: Theorem 4.1 preserves all four parts: measurable bijective isometry and pushforward invariance, mode rank and median membership, monotonicity along an ordered-profile curve, and characterization under strong negative type of the metric. The scalar rank with an extra u argument in part (c) and the separability-only opening remain printed source wording.

Theorem 5.1 preserves Assumptions 1-2, all anchors and real thresholds, the Gaussian-process limit and the complete ball-indicator covariance. Theorem 5.2 preserves the root-n uniform stochastic order; it is not a central limit theorem. Theorem 5.3 retains explicit nonemptiness, Assumptions 1-3 and the two-sided Hausdorff conclusion.

Theorem 6.1 preserves H0, Assumptions 1/4/5/6 and the exact random-series law with averaged pointwise covariance eigenvalues. Theorem 6.2 retains the discrepancy-defined alternative sequence and oracle-cutoff power (30).

Theorem 6.3 retains all three clauses: pointwise CDF convergence at continuity points, null quantile consistency with local continuity/strict increase, and permutation power with the mixture quantile and both root-total-size balance restrictions. The reversed m,n subscript and the omitted repeated K limit in the last clause remain as printed.
source_passages: All 28 source entries and four auxiliary passages were checked. The totally bounded separable metric model, Borel law, distance CDF, independent-copy random-anchor interpretation and generalized inverse match pages 7-8. The signed quantile integral and expit rank are distinct from absolute Wasserstein cost. The support-constrained median argmax and all-radii transport mode match pages 9/11.

The population and empirical profiles, leave-one-out random-anchor rank term, full-sample fixed-anchor term and sample-restricted median argmax remain separate. Assumption 1 retains its covering-entropy limit. Assumption 2 retains continuous densities, anchorwise lower bounds and a uniform upper bound. The ball-indicator class, Hausdorff distance and literal individual-median separation match pages 12-14.

The two-sample model and four empirical profiles match pages 14-15, including the distinct within-sample denominators. The weighted statistic retains integration against du and its nm/(n+m) factor. Weight convergence (25), population discrepancy, identifying-class discussion, permutation construction and all quantile definitions match pages 15-18.

Assumption 4 retains uniform consistency, boundedness and Lipschitz conditions without adding positivity. Assumption 5 is distinct from Assumption 2 and does not expressly require continuous densities. Assumption 6 gives limiting sample balance. The shrinking discrepancy alternatives, oracle power, null covariance law, mixture law and permutation power retain their separate definitions.
findings.dependency_review: All 43 direct uses, 70 related connections, 28 local reach sets and every reported path were checked. Strong negative type and transport mode reach only Theorem 4.1. Rank/median assumptions do not propagate into the two-sample branch. Assumptions 2 and 5 remain distinct. The oracle cutoff depends on the null law without importing the alternative-power object. The null, empirical permutation and mixture critical values remain separate, as do oracle and permutation power. Proof references do not add supplement dependencies.
findings.names_and_highlights: All 28 interface titles use source natural-language keywords. Source types, labels, naming contexts, independent-copy and weight-convergence application passages, and selectors were compared with original text and related same-paper statements. Assumptions retain their original identity. The null law remains a theorem excerpt rather than an invented numbered definition.
findings.source_limitations: The 22 existing notes preserve the incorrect unrestricted-h strong-negative-type statement, metric versus powered metric, density-boundary issue, individual-median separation versus prose, extra u on ranks, unbound x in (22), inconsistent permutation split, omitted weight positivity, unspecified covariance operator, use of contiguous terminology, composite-power convention, total boundedness versus separability, overloaded empirical profiles, distinct density assumptions, omitted convergence topology, inverse endpoints, unrestricted monotone-transform prose, argmax existence, permutation indexing/limit clauses, redundant balance conditions, weight recomputation and different quantile domains. Source review preserves the original mathematical claims and does not certify their correctness.
findings.changes: Corrected an escaped ASCII bell to literal LaTeX alpha in D25 naming_context, matching page 16. Every regenerated JSON value was compared; this is the sole content correction. The original theorem statements, definition bodies, dependency graph and counts are unchanged. The prior audit and artifacts are archived in review-history/before-naming-context-correction/. The per-paper rebuild now resolves the fixed local PDF and preserves shared-page clipping; earlier scripts are archived, and the finalizer docstring correctly says seven theorems.
findings.validation: Independent inventory and census validators pass; all six regenerated artifacts match saved bytes. Source identity, exact main-text heading enumeration, source boundary, graph sets, selectors and artifact hashes supplement the completed manual source review.
